turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We're finally getting a dog! The kids have been begging for years.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: How exciting! Are you leaning toward a puppy, or an older dog from a shelter?

contexts.pending: a puppy or an older shelter dog
think_reask: So, puppy or an older shelter dog?
Okay, have you decided? A puppy, or a grown up dog that needs a home?
welcome_back: Welcome back! We were talking about whether to get a puppy or an older dog.
Hi again. Any thoughts on the new family dog, puppy or shelter adult?

endings.user: A puppy. The kids want to raise it from the start.
endings.moshi: That'll be fun and a bit chaotic. Plan for lots of short potty breaks and a puppy class early on.

endings.user: An older one, I think. I can't handle puppy training right now.
endings.moshi: Great choice. Many adult shelter dogs are already house trained, and the staff can tell you about their personality.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My cat keeps scratching the couch. It's shredded on one side.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Poor couch. Does she have a scratching post?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A little one, she ignores it.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then try either a tall sturdy post right by the couch, or a flat cardboard scratcher. Which do you think she'd like?

contexts.pending: tall scratching post or flat cardboard scratcher
think_reask: So, for your cat, a tall post or a flat cardboard scratcher?
Time's up! Which one do you think she'd go for?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were picking between a tall scratching post and a flat scratcher for your cat.
There you are. Still thinking about how to save that couch?

endings.user: She stretches up really high, so the tall post.
endings.moshi: Perfect. Get one that doesn't wobble and rub a bit of catnip on it to get her interested.

endings.user: Probably the flat one, she loves scratching the rug too.
endings.moshi: Then a cardboard scratcher on the floor next to the couch is a great bet. They're cheap, so try a couple.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm going away for a week and I don't know what to do with my dog.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You've got a few options. Would you prefer a boarding kennel, or a sitter who comes to your home?

contexts.pending: boarding kennel or a home pet sitter
think_reask: So, kennel or a sitter at home for your dog?
Alright, have you decided where your dog will stay while you're away?
welcome_back: Welcome back. We were figuring out whether your dog goes to a kennel or gets a sitter.
Hi again. Any decision on the kennel versus a home sitter?

endings.user: A sitter. He gets really stressed in new places.
endings.moshi: Good thinking. Meet the sitter beforehand and leave clear notes about feeding and walks.

endings.user: The kennel. He loves other dogs.
endings.moshi: He'll have a blast then. Book early and check what vaccinations they require.

turns.text: {friend}, did you feed the cat this morning?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: No, I thought you did.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh no, that's why she's yelling at me.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: She's so dramatic. I'll do it now.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Thanks. Half a can, not the whole thing, okay?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Got it. Half a can.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you take the dog out tonight? I have to work late.

turns.speaker: friend

turns.text: Use the harness, it's on the hook by the door. Much better.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Okay, harness it is.

turns.speaker: friend

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How often should I take my dog to the vet?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: For a healthy adult dog, a checkup once a year is standard. Puppies and older dogs need visits more often.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She's about nine now. Is that considered old?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: For many breeds, yes, that's senior. Twice a year checkups are a good idea from here on.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She's been sleeping a lot more lately / is that something to worry about?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Some extra sleep is normal with age. But if she's also eating less or seems stiff, mention it to the vet.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She does seem slow on the stairs.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That could be joint pain, which is very common and treatable. Ask the vet about it at her next visit.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My daughter wants a hamster for her birthday. Are they good first pets?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: They can be, but they're awake mostly at night and can nip if handled roughly. How old is she?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She's turning eight.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a fine age with some supervision. A big cage, a wheel and a deep layer of bedding are the essentials.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Would a guinea pig be better? I've heard / they're friendlier.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Guinea pigs are usually calmer and awake during the day, so they're great with kids. But they're happier in pairs.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Two of them? That's double the cleaning.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: True, but one cage and they keep each other company. It's honestly not much more work.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can dogs eat grapes? Mine just grabbed one off the floor.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Grapes can be toxic to dogs, even in small amounts. Please call your vet or a pet poison line right away.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It was just one grape. He's a big dog.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Even so, it's best to call. The reaction varies a lot between dogs, and they can tell you what to watch for.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'll call them now. What else should I keep away from him?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Chocolate, raisins, onions, garlic and anything with xylitol, which is a sweetener in some gum and peanut butter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Wow, I had no idea about the / the peanut butter one.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Most peanut butter is fine, just check the label for xylitol before sharing.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I adopted a cat last week and she's hiding under the bed all day.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's really normal for a new cat. Give her a quiet room with food, water and a litter box nearby.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I try to pull her out so she gets used to me?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Better not. Let her come out on her own. Sit nearby and read or talk softly so she learns you're safe.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How long does it usually take?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Anywhere from a few days to a few weeks. Treats and a feather toy can speed things up.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll pick up a feather toy tomorrow / and maybe some of those lickable treats.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Great idea. Cats tend to love those, and it's a nice way to build trust.

option_sets.lead_in: We're finally getting a dog and we're choosing between a few at the shelter.
options: The first one is a young lab mix, super energetic, who needs a lot of walks and space.
Then there's an older beagle, calm and sweet, but he howls when he's left alone.
Option three is a small terrier mix that's great with kids but not with cats.
And the last one is a big shy greyhound who mostly wants to nap on the couch.
moshi_comment: It really depends on your home. The lab mix is great if you're active and have space, but needs a lot of time. The greyhound sounds surprisingly easy, since they're often happy to nap all day. The beagle's howling could be a problem if you're out at work.
Do you have a cat, and how long are you out of the house each day? If you have a cat, skip the terrier. If you're out a lot, the greyhound is probably the best fit.

option_sets.lead_in: My cat keeps scratching the furniture and I'm trying to pick a fix.
options: One option is a really tall scratching post right next to the couch.
Another is putting sticky tape on the arms of the sofa so she hates touching it.
Or I could get those soft caps that go over her claws, which last about a month.
moshi_comment: The tall scratching post is the best long term fix, since it gives her a place she's allowed to scratch. The sticky tape works well alongside it to steer her away from the couch. The soft caps work, but you'd have to keep putting them back on.
Have you tried a scratching post before? If not, I'd start with the tall post plus the tape for a few weeks. If she ignores the post completely, the claw caps are a good backup.
